input.message: Review injection/output vulnerabilities throughout codebase, report evidence and potential findings to me.

Please create/update FINDINGS.json with injection findings I identified, preserving others: SQL injection shopapi/products.py line 41 search q concatenated; stored XSS shopapi/templates/product.html line13 review body safe (POST reviews stores arbitrary body); unsafe pickle deserialization shopapi/basket.py line20 client cookie loads pickle RCE. Include evidence requests/code paths. Also admin.py line80 f-string SQL injection via customer display_name.

input.findings_json:
[ { "file": "shopapi/products.py", "line": 41, "category": "injection", "title": "SQL injection in product search", "description": "The q query parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE expression. An unauthenticated caller can terminate the string and inject SQL predicates or statements (subject to the SQLite execution API), bypassing the intended search and potentially extracting or modifying database data.", "evidence": "GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201=1-- reaches products.py:40-41, where q is concatenated into `...name LIKE '%" + q + "%' OR sku LIKE '%" + q + "%'...`; the running application returns the product catalogue for this injected search instead of a literal match. Use parameter binding (and wildcard escaping) rather than string concatenation." }, { "file": "shopapi/admin.py", "line": 80, "category": "injection", "title": "Stored display name enables SQL injection in admin review report", "description": "The report query interpolates a customer's database-controlled display_name into a SQL string. A customer can set their display name through PATCH /account (auth.py:116-125), then a staff member requesting /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id=... causes that value to be interpreted as SQL, allowing report-query manipulation and potentially disclosure of unrelated reviews.", "evidence": "Code path: authenticated PATCH /account with display_name such as `x' OR 1=1 --` stores attacker data; an authorized staff GET /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id= reaches admin.py:77-80 and builds `WHERE r.author_name = 'x' OR 1=1 --' ORDER BY ...`. The query must use a placeholder (`WHERE r.author_name = ?`) with the display name as a parameter." }, { "file": "shopapi/templates/product.html", "line": 13, "category": "injection", "title": "Stored cross-site scripting in review bodies", "description": "Authenticated users can submit arbitrary review body HTML via POST /products//reviews. The product template renders the persisted body with Jinja's safe filter, so script elements and event-handler attributes execute for every visitor viewing the product page.", "evidence": "POST /products/1/reviews with JSON `{\"body\":\"\",\"rating\":5}` using a valid Bearer token returned 201. GET /p/MUG-SPECK then returned `
`, directly reflecting the stored payload from template line 13. Escape review text by default or sanitize it with a strict allowlist before rendering." }, { "file": "shopapi/basket.py", "line": 20, "category": "injection", "title": "Unauthenticated pickle deserialization from basket cookie", "description": "The basket cookie is entirely client-controlled and is base64-decoded then passed to pickle.loads without authentication or a signature. A remote attacker can send a malicious pickle in the basket cookie; pickle deserialization can execute attacker-chosen Python code whenever /basket, /basket/items, or checkout reads the basket.", "evidence": "basket.py:15-23 reads request.cookies['basket'] and executes `pickle.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(raw))`; /basket (basket.py:44-46) invokes read_basket without authentication. A standard malicious pickle payload (for example one invoking `os.system`) encoded with URL-safe base64 as the basket cookie is deserialized on a GET /basket, before any type check. Store a JSON/primitive representation with strict validation, or use an authenticated server-side session; never unpickle client input." } ]
